question:
(i) Explain why the ray approximation used in optical instruments is valid when the wavelength of light is very small compared with the aperture of the instrument.
(ii) Use Huygens Principle to justify the relation between wavefronts and rays in this case.

options.A:
(i) Ray optics is valid when wavelength is comparable to aperture, so diffraction is maximum.
(ii) Rays are parallel to wavefronts.
options.B:
(i) Ray approximation is valid because light has no wave nature.
(ii) Wavefronts do not determine ray direction.
options.C:
(i) When wavelength is much smaller than aperture, diffraction is negligible and light follows nearly straight paths, so geometrical optics applies.
(ii) Huygens Principle gives new wavefronts as envelopes of secondary wavelets. Rays are normals to wavefronts; with negligible spreading, these normals give well-defined ray directions.
options.D:
(i) Ray approximation is valid only for very small apertures.
(ii) Rays are tangential to wavefronts.
